constraint: Must maintain knee implant function within clinical specifications
mechanism: Routine intraoperative microbiological screening detects occult periprosthetic joint infections that would otherwise be missed, enabling timely antibiotic or surgical treatment and thereby reducing the risk of subsequent implant failure.
intervention: Implementation of routine intraoperative microbiological sampling during presumed aseptic revision arthroplasty.
expected_effect: Improved implant survival (reduced rate of revision or failure) compared to no routine screening, due to identification and treatment of unexpected infections.
falsification_test: A randomized controlled trial comparing implant survival between patients undergoing routine intraoperative cultures versus standard care, with a null hypothesis of no difference; or a retrospective cohort analysis showing no significant survival advantage after adjusting for confounders.
mechanism_source_span: "This study aimed to evaluate the association between routine intraoperative microbiological screening and implant survival in presumed aseptic revision arthroplasty."

source_evidence.source_title: Routine intraoperative infection testing in presumed aseptic hip and knee revision: a matched cohort retrospective study.
source_evidence.source_span: Introduction Periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs) complicate 1-2% of primary and up to 4% of revision arthroplasties, and their diagnosis remains challenging due to the lack of a diagnostic gold standard. Differentiating PJI from aseptic failure is particularly difficult in low-grade or biofilm-related infections.
